decisions.decision: Treat the following as already closed and do not re-implement, rename or re-prove them: the three top-level tests in internal/release (TestCompileFoundationBaselineContract, TestBundleImmutableRouteAndRollback, TestContractAndPromotionGateRejectDriftAndStaleEvidence) and the fourteen in internal/contracts (TestSchemasAndFixtures, TestCanonicalTaskStateMigration, TestCanonicalTaskStateInvariants, TestHistoricalBootstrapRecordsAndIndexes, TestActiveEvidenceIndex, TestCanonicalTaskStateNegativeMatrix, TestSchemasRejectSensitiveFieldNames, the four TestDeploymentPreflightLedger* tests, TestDeploymentPreflightLedgerPassesWithAWellFormedRecord, TestTaskPacketsValidate, TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline). V2-009 already proves contract/declaration-set schema validity, capability-id bijection between foundation.json and foundation-capabilities.json, contract_ref and release equality, the baseline invariant (all twelve capabilities preview with empty evidence_ids), the anti-fabrication invariant (stable requires evidence plus documentation.stable), evidence-id resolution against the ledger, documentation anchor resolution (path#anchor occurring exactly once), evidence_schema path existence, owner_surfaces resolution against declared OpenAPI paths, and make-target resolution for verification entries. V2-010 already proves, by BFS over the domain state machine, that CompleteRequirementFromRelease is reachable only from evaluating and only with a valid StableReleaseProof. V2-021 adds only the gaps named in d2 through d12.
decisions.rationale: Measured, not assumed: devbox run --pure -- go test -v ./internal/release ./internal/contracts reports exactly 3 and 14 passing top-level tests at HEAD 576019e. Re-asserting covered behaviour spends implementer context and inflates the release evidence without moving any M5 completion condition.

decisions.decision: The single most important measured fact for this task: the existing 'docs drift' claim does not detect docs drift. PromotionGate's signature is PromotionGate(bundle Bundle, control domain.EffectiveControlResult, permit domain.PermitDecision); no documentation bytes ever reach it, and domain.ReleaseCandidate.CanPromote only compares the candidate's DocsDigest against the DocsDigest recorded on each CapabilityEvidence. A probe that set both candidate.DocsDigest and evidence[0].DocsDigest to the fabricated string 'drifted-docs' promoted to status stable with a nil error. TestContractAndPromotionGateRejectDriftAndStaleEvidence only mutates one side, so it proves internal consistency of a candidate, not agreement with the source tree. V2-021's core deliverable is therefore an assembly boundary that derives every digest from source bytes plus a source re-verification at the gate, so that no caller can assert a digest.
decisions.rationale: The M5 completion condition is 'docsだけのdriftでもpromotionが止まる'. A gate that never reads documentation bytes cannot satisfy it, and shipping the existing test as evidence for that condition would be a fabricated claim. The probe was executed against copies of internal/domain and internal/release in a scratch module, so no repository file was modified to measure it.

decisions.decision: Define the Release Candidate bundle's immutable digest as a canonical manifest over declared members grouped into seven roles: contract (contracts/release-contract/**), schema (contracts/schemas/**), api-contract (contracts/openapi/**), implementation-manifest (ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.lock), migration (firestore.indexes.json), configuration (devbox.json, firebase.json), documentation (docs/preview/**.md, docs/stable/**.md). A member is (role, repository-relative path, sha256 of its bytes). BundleDigest is sha256 over the framing 'role\x00path\x00hexdigest\n' for all members sorted by (role, path); DocsDigest is the same framing restricted to role documentation; ContractDigest keeps its current meaning, sha256 of contracts/release-contract/foundation.json bytes as produced by CompileContract. CompileContract's signature is unchanged: the assembly passes the documentation framing bytes as its docs argument, so CompiledContract.DocsDigest equals the doc-set digest by construction.
decisions.rationale: release-contract.md section 4 item 8 requires implementation, schema, migration, configuration and user documentation to be promotable as one version, so the digest must cover exactly those roles rather than one opaque blob. Path-prefixed framing makes the digest insensitive to filesystem enumeration order and sensitive to a rename, which a concatenated content hash is not. Reusing CompileContract's docs argument avoids a signature change that would ripple into V2-009's contract_baseline_test.go, which passes docs/preview/capabilities.md bytes directly and asserts only Version and the capability id list. A local candidate has no built binary digest: the implementation identity at M5-local is the source manifest, and the binary digest is V2-022 (live image) and V2-034 (signed update bundle). This must be stated in the work report, not implied.

decisions.decision: Prove the docs drift gate in three layers and label each one honestly. L1, hermetic semantics: build a synthetic repository tree under t.TempDir(), assemble a candidate, promote it through the gate, then flip one byte of one documentation member, re-assemble, and assert (a) DocsDigest changed, (b) VerifySource(bundle, root) refuses and names the drifted member path, (c) the previously assembled candidate's capability evidence is no longer fresh so CanPromote fails, (d) Pipeline.Promote returns an error and leaves Router generation unchanged, and (e) as the negative control, flipping a byte in a file that matches no role glob leaves BundleDigest and DocsDigest unchanged. L2, real-tree conformance: assemble from the repository root and record the digests. L3, CI enforcement: a docs-only commit moves the docs component's evidence key, so make candidate-affected refuses the candidate until fresh docs evidence exists; this task's own docs edits produce that observation, and the before/after docs component key is recorded in the evidence rather than synthesised.
decisions.rationale: An absence assertion with no positive control proves nothing, which is why (e) is mandatory: without it, a test that hashes the whole tree would pass the same assertions while making every unrelated commit a docs drift. Splitting L1 from L3 keeps the claim precise: L1 is a property of the release core, L3 is a property of the selective-CI ledger, and neither implies the other.

decisions.decision: Make the evidence-key soundness boundary self-declaring instead of silent. internal/ci/planner.go evidenceKey() hashes, for each component, the files matching its roots, its public_contracts, its contract_dependencies, and the public_contracts of its declared dependencies, plus ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock unconditionally. For the release component that closure is internal/release/**, contracts/** (via the contracts dependency's public_contracts), and those four files. Therefore the contract, schema, api-contract and implementation-manifest roles are guarded (any drift moves the release evidence key and re-runs the release component), while the documentation, migration and configuration roles are not. A test in internal/release parses ci/components.json directly (no import of internal/ci) to recompute that closure, and asserts that every bundle member is either inside it or listed in an explicit UnguardedMembers allowlist; the test fails both when a member is neither, and when an allowlisted member becomes guarded.
decisions.rationale: Reading real repository files from a component whose evidence key does not cover them is exactly the evidence-key defect that V2-045 was opened for. It cannot be fixed here, because the fix is a ci/components.json edit and ci/** is in all_on_change while ci/components.json is hashed into all 23 component keys, and the V2-040 candidate-aggregate record pins all 23 keys in its check summaries. Encoding the partition as a machine-checked allowlist converts an invisible unsoundness into a declared one that the fix must delete, so the escalation cannot be forgotten.

decisions.decision: Bind the candidate's capability set to the compiled contract at assembly. AssembleCandidate derives ReleaseCandidate.Capabilities from CompiledContract.Capabilities in contract order, and VerifyCandidateAgainstContract refuses any candidate whose capability set is not exactly the compiled set. Prove three cases: the assembled Foundation candidate declares exactly the twelve baseline ids; evidence for eleven of twelve is refused with the missing capability named; and a hand-built candidate declaring one capability is refused even though its internal digests agree.
decisions.rationale: Measured: a candidate declaring the single capability 'healthz', bound to the real foundation.json contract digest and the real docs digest, promoted to status stable with a nil error while the contract declares twelve. domain.CanPromote iterates r.Capabilities, so the completeness invariant is only as strong as whoever populated that slice. The M5 completion condition '全機能Evidenceを持つcandidateだけStableになる' is unmet until the slice is derived rather than supplied.

decisions.decision: Keep the promotion and rollback path inside internal/release for V2-021 and escalate the canonical surface. Measured: outside internal/domain and internal/release there is no reference to ReleaseCandidate anywhere in internal/application, internal/store, internal/api or internal/reconciler, so there is no application or store release surface to route the transition through. Do not create one here (internal/application/**, internal/store/** and internal/api/** are prohibited): instead introduce release.Pipeline over the package's existing Store port and Router, and escalate the canonical release aggregate, its UnitOfWork and its event/outbox projection as E2, since V2-022 needs it for a live promotion.
decisions.rationale: product_orchestrator's brief asks what to show through application and store. The honest answer measured from the tree is that the path does not exist, and inventing it inside V2-021 would add three components (application, store-memory, store-firestore, plus api) to a task whose gate component is release, while V2-019 holds the reconciler and application boundary open. Escalating with the exact missing types is the tech-lead action; guessing a schema for Firestore release documents is not.

decisions.decision: Fix the measured rollback ping-pong and express rollback at route and artifact level only. Measured: after promoting v1 then v2, Router.Rollback moved stable to v1 and set PreviousStableDigest to v2, and a second Rollback returned stable to v2 with a nil error at generation 6, re-promoting a rolled-back digest without passing the gate. After the change, Rollback moves stable back to the previous stable, clears the forward pointer, and records a RollbackRecord (repository, from digest, to digest, reason, at); a second consecutive Rollback is refused, and moving forward again requires SetPreview plus Promote through the full gate. Do not add a domain transition: domain.ReleaseAssembling, ReleasePreviewDeployed, ReleaseRejected and ReleaseRollback are constants that no transition function produces, and internal/domain non-test files are prohibited. Record that as escalation E3, not as a decision this task made.
decisions.rationale: A rollback that another rollback can undo is not a rollback; it is a toggle, and it lets a version that was withdrawn for a regression become stable again with no evidence and no permit. Fixing it inside Router is a two-line behaviour change that TestBundleImmutableRouteAndRollback still passes unchanged, because that test rolls back exactly once. Reaching the domain rollback status would require a new domain function, which is a cross-boundary redesign and belongs to product_orchestrator.

decisions.decision: Chain the docs drift gate to Requirement completion rather than re-proving V2-010's reachability result. Show four things: a refused gate returns the zero StableReleaseProof, so CompleteRequirementFromRelease refuses it with ErrEvidenceIncomplete and a docs-drifted candidate can therefore never complete a Requirement; a completed Requirement's StableSnapshot BundleDigest and EvidenceDigest equal the bundle held in the Store under the candidate id, so completion always references a release that exists; after completion the router's stable digest equals the completed snapshot's candidate digest and the default documentation channel resolves to stable; and if the completion step fails, the router generation is unchanged, so there is no half-promoted state.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 2 requires 'completed RequirementはStable Releaseを参照する' as a standing property, and release-contract.md section 4 requires the Stable document entry to become the default in the same step as completion. V2-010 proved the transition is reachable only from evaluating with a valid proof; what is unproven is that the proof a real gate emits is bound to a stored bundle and to the document route, which is precisely the M5 'Requirement completed判定' deliverable.

decisions.decision: Machine-verify Preview and Stable documentation routing with deterministic checks and no AI review. The checks are: every relative markdown link in the doc set resolves to an existing file, and every path#anchor link resolves to exactly one occurrence; the capability anchor set in docs/preview/capabilities.md is bijective with the contract's capability ids in both directions (V2-009 checks only contract-to-document); each channel index declares a machine-parsable release marker, the preview marker equals the contract's release string, and the stable marker is 'none' exactly while no capability has status stable; the preview channel contains the four required sections (difference from Stable, known issues, how to return to Stable, evidence still missing for promotion); no document under docs/stable/** links into docs/preview/**; and fenced code blocks are extracted and checked against a command allowlist, with the extractor proven on a synthetic fixture because the real doc set currently contains zero fenced blocks.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 4 requires link and version checking, source-schema cross-checking, safe code-block execution, and the presence of difference, known issues and rollback in Preview docs, and states explicitly that AI review does not replace schema and link checks; the task's non_goals repeat that. A check over an empty set is vacuous, so the code-block extractor must be exercised on a fixture that does contain blocks, and the real-tree assertion must be the falsifiable 'zero blocks now, any future block must be allowlisted'.

decisions.decision: Mature retention eligibility here, as docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 assigns to V2-021, as a pure function with three independent refusals and one positive case: a version is retention-eligible only when it is neither the current stable nor the previous stable route target, and its contract-declared rollback window has closed against an injected clock, and no Requirement's StableSnapshot references it. Execution of the deletion (GC) stays with V2-034 at M8.
decisions.rationale: release-contract.md section 5 requires the user documents of a rollback target to be retained until the rollback window closes, and validation.md section 8 forbids expiring evidence on the clock alone. Three separate refusals are needed because a single boolean would let a passing test hide two of the three reasons.

decisions.decision: Do not import internal/update or internal/ci from internal/release, in test files or otherwise, and assert that with a go/ast import guard over the package. The release component declares dependencies on domain and contracts only; an import of update or ci would create a component edge that ci/components.json does not record, so a change there would neither select the release component nor move its evidence key. The relationship between a route rollback and update.Switch's atomic channel symlink rollback is documented in docs/operations/release-local.md instead of being coded.
decisions.rationale: Hidden component edges are the mechanism by which a green selective CI stops meaning anything. Writing the relationship down keeps the operator-visible fact while keeping the manifest true.

decisions.decision: Limit documentation edits to docs/preview/index.md, docs/preview/stable-diff.md and docs/stable/index.md, and prohibit docs/preview/capabilities.md and docs/preview/README.md. Measured: capabilities.md carries the twelve anchors that TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline resolves with an exactly-once assertion, so editing it risks breaking a V2-009 claim for no gain; the checks this task adds need only a release marker in each channel index and the four required sections in stable-diff.md, which currently has the difference and missing-evidence content but no known-issues and no return-to-Stable section, and neither index carries a release marker.
decisions.rationale: Narrow allowed paths are how a docs change stays reviewable, and the anchor set is load-bearing for another task's evidence.

decisions.decision: Forbid any digest value from appearing inside the doc set. Recording a doc-set digest in a file that is itself a documentation member creates a fixpoint that no assembly can satisfy. The bundle, contract and doc-set digests are recorded only in the in-memory candidate and in the evidence record's artifact_refs; docs/operations/release-local.md, which is not a documentation member, records the algorithm and never a value.
decisions.rationale: This is the failure mode most likely to be introduced by an implementer trying to make the drift check 'visible in the docs', and it would be discovered only as an unfixable test.

decisions.decision: Produce exactly one evidence record, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-021-release.json, with id ev-v2-021-release, task_id V2-021 as the producer, component release and result passed, one check per acceptance item with the argv actually executed and its timeout, artifact_refs carrying the bundle digest, the contract digest and the doc-set digest of the real-tree Foundation candidate, and a check whose summary reports both the release and the docs component evidence keys read with make evidence-keys on the final tree at which make check is green. Register exactly one entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the record file's bytes.
decisions.rationale: Sol's common acceptance: the definition of done is the pair (record registered in the index, ledger test green), not merely that the tests passed. The record needs the docs key as well as the release key because this task's claims span both components while the schema carries one evidence_key, and the M5 gate row in the DAG names release.

decisions.decision: State the V2-022 boundary claim by claim, in the work report and in release-local.md. V2-021 does not and may not claim: that this Foundation Repository was made a Preview target; that any Preview environment was deployed; that any capability was exercised in a Preview environment (all twelve remain status preview with empty evidence_ids, so the assembled Foundation candidate is provably not promotable); that a Preview was intentionally broken and a Requirement resumed on the previous Stable; that a real Provider CLI, a real GCP project or a real credential was used; or that a Stable release exists. What V2-021 claims is only that the local release core refuses the wrong candidate and accepts the right one, over synthetic trees and over the real repository tree, with no deploy and no promotion.
decisions.rationale: G3 rejects local, emulator and fake evidence as a substitute for a live completion condition, and component naming is how the gate tells them apart: release is local, release-live-dogfood is V2-022. An implementer who reports 'promotion and rollback verified' without that boundary hands the M5 gate a fabricated claim.

decisions.decision: Determinism is an acceptance property. Every new test uses t.TempDir() fixtures, an injected clock, a per-test context deadline, one top-level function per journey and no package-level mutable state; no fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence, no background timer, and no dependence on another test's order. Do not create test/journeys/ and do not edit ci/components.json; journeys live in internal/release/journey_test.go.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a result that varied, so a test that needs a retry to pass is a stop-and-escalate condition. ValidateTracked requires exactly one owning component per tracked file, so test/journeys/** cannot exist without the prohibited ci/components.json edit and make ownership, part of make check, would fail.

verification: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/release (timeout 600s): the 3 pre-existing tests still pass under their current names, plus the new bundle, source-verification, docs-routing, retention, pipeline and journey tests.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -race ./internal/release (timeout 600s): Store, Router and Pipeline stay race-clean under their existing mutexes.
devbox run --pure -- make component-release (timeout 900s): the release component check target (./internal/release ./internal/domain) is green, confirming no domain regression.
devbox run --pure -- make component-docs (timeout 300s): no TODO(ci) marker is introduced by the three edited documents.
devbox run --pure -- make docs (timeout 300s): the deleted-numbered-document link guard still passes over the edited documents.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts (timeout 600s): TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline still resolves all twelve capability anchors exactly once after the documentation edits, TestTaskPacketsValidate accepts both V2-021 packets, and TestActiveEvidenceIndex accepts the registered evidence record.
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys (timeout 900s) on the final formatted tree, to read the release and docs component evidence keys the record must carry.
devbox run --pure -- make check (timeout 2400s), run again after the evidence commit so that gitleaks git scans the committed history.
devbox run --pure -- make candidate-affected (timeout 1800s) after the commit, to observe that the docs component's key moved and required fresh docs evidence.
risks: A docs-only commit does not select the release component. Measured from ci/components.json and internal/ci/planner.go Affected(): the docs component has no public_contracts, so nothing couples docs/** to the release component's contract_dependencies, and its check target is only 'rg -n TODO(ci)'. The new drift tests therefore run under make check and make test but not under a docs-only selective CI run. This is escalation E1; it must be stated in the evidence and in release-local.md, and must not be described as CI-enforced.

The bundle's documentation, migration and configuration roles read files outside the release component's evidence-key closure. The UnguardedMembers allowlist makes that visible, but it does not make it sound; an implementer who deletes an allowlist entry to make a test pass would silently remove the boundary. Review must reject that.

Changing Router.Rollback is a behaviour change to a function that TestBundleImmutableRouteAndRollback asserts. That test rolls back once and must keep passing byte-for-byte; if it needs editing, the change is wrong.

Deriving ReleaseCandidate.Capabilities from the compiled contract makes the real-tree Foundation candidate non-promotable, because all twelve baseline capabilities have empty evidence_ids. That is the correct outcome and must be asserted as such, not worked around by fabricating capability evidence for the real tree.

The release marker added to docs/preview/index.md and docs/stable/index.md is parsed by a test. A free-prose sentence that a later documentation edit rewords would break the check; the marker must be a fixed, documented line format.

.agents/v2/evidence/index.json is being edited concurrently by another implementer. Add only the single ev-v2-021-release entry, never rewrite or reorder another task's entry, and recompute evidence_hash on the final bytes after any rebase.

docs/architecture/technology.md, docs/architecture/validation.md, docs/operations/runner-local.md and other .agents/v2/evidence/** records are held open by another implementer, and .agents/v2/packets/V2-019-*.json by another tech lead. Touching any of them is out of scope and will conflict.

Scope creep into internal/application and internal/store is the most likely way this task exceeds its retry budget of 2. The canonical release surface does not exist; the correct response to needing it is escalation E2, not implementation.
